title: Tire and Frame Clearance Guide
intro: With particularly wide tires, the question often arises whether they will fit in the frame. Because bicycle models vary widely, we cannot check every frame. The tables below provide reference tire widths and diameters from Schwalbe charts. Compare these values with the clearance available in your frame, fork, and stays before installation. Actual dimensions can vary with rim inner width, tire pressure, load, and the tire and rim combination.

measurement.title: Understand dimensions A, B and C before checking frame clearance
measurement.intro: A is the horizontal maximum width. Schwalbe reports B and C as diameter values: maximum diameter and shoulder diameter at maximum width. The diagram uses vertical arrows to show the corresponding upper measurement points from the rim shoulder reference.
measurement.important: Important: B and C are not the one-sided height from the rim edge. To estimate that height above the rim shoulder, subtract the rim bead seat diameter from the reported diameter and divide the result by two.

width.title: Maximum tire width
width.body: The widest outside-to-outside measurement across the mounted tire, measured from outside lug to outside lug at maximum air pressure. Use A to check side-to-side clearance between the tire and the frame, fork, or stays.

diameter.title: Maximum outer diameter
diameter.body: Schwalbe's maximum-diameter value for the mounted tire and wheel. It is the full outside diameter across the highest point of the inflated tread or tread lug. Use B to check the largest overall radial envelope. For one-sided height above the rim shoulder, use (B - bead seat diameter) / 2.

shoulder.title: Shoulder diameter at maximum width
shoulder.body: Schwalbe's shoulder diameter measured where the tire reaches its maximum width. It is the full diameter across that shoulder level, usually near the outer shoulder lugs on a knobby tire. For one-sided height above the rim shoulder, use (C - bead seat diameter) / 2.

circumference.title: Exact Circumference Guide
circumference.intro: Exact tire circumferences are often required for precise programming of a bike computer. Wheel circumference varies with inner rim width, puncture protection, air pressure, and weight load. The values below are approximate references, not a substitute for measuring the mounted tire.
circumference.test: For precise programming, we recommend a simple rolling test with the rider in the saddle: align the front-wheel valve at the bottom 6 o'clock position, mark the floor, roll the bike forward in as straight a line as possible until the valve returns to 6 o'clock, and measure the distance between the two marks.
